newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-NATAL SEE THEMSELVES AS UNDERDOGS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NATAL SEE THEMSELVES AS UNDERDOGS.

text.p: Natal, the first-class champions of South African domestic cricket two seasons ago, now regard themselves as outsiders for the title as they enter the new four-day Supersport Series at Kingsmead on Friday.
Their first match of the season is against a much-improved Border side but Natal go into it with a severely depleted line- up.

"It's a very different set-up for us this season. We're missing eight guys at the moment from our regular team of last year with five players in India, Shaun Pollock still injured and both Malcolm Marshall and Ross Veenstra having left us," Natal coach Graham Ford told Reuters.

"From our point of view, we're going out there to enjoy it and to allow the young guys to see what they can produce. Last year, we were out to defend the trophy and we were favourites. This year, we are outsiders looking to pull a few upsets."
Ford views Border as a side which is improving noticeably each season with several young players of great potential.

"They have a pretty balanced attack with good frontline bowlers in West Indian Vasbert Drakes and Makhaya Ntini and more than adequate support from Frans Cronje, Piet Strydom and Brendan Horan and the left-arm spin of Ian Howell. They also bat a long way down and have real experience in Peter Kirsten."
Ford feels that Ntini and Horan in particular are both on track for successful cricketing careers:

"Makhaya looks a fine young prospect...he's very competitive and bowls with a lively amount of pace. Horan I saw in the Castle Cup last year and he lookd very useful... he moves the ball both ways and hits the seam."
The only worry for Ford going into Natal's opening first- class fixture has been the amount of rainfall in Durban during the week.
"I think we can expect a good four-day wicket which should produce a close contest, as long as the rain doesn't greatly hamper both the preparations and the match itself."
In the other Supersport Series matches starting on Friday, defending champions Western Province take on Northern Transvaal in Cape Town while Boland host Griqualand West in Paarl.
Like Natal, Western Province are missing several players through either national commitments in India or injury.
Left-arm spinner Paul Adams is still suffering from a groin strain and all-rounder Jacques Kallis (back stress fracture) will only be able to play as a batsman in about six weeks.
However former Eastern Province left-arm pace bowler Brett Schultz will make his first-class debut for Province on Friday after returning to club cricket action over the weekend from an ankle injury.
Despite the non-availability of six players, John Commins' side still enjoys the luxury of four cricketers with test experience, as well as one-day internationals Eric Simons and Dave Rundle.
